sections.heading: Upfront, Honest and Family Owned
body: J M. called Linnebur “Upfront, honest, and great pricing,” and said it “continues all the way through to the end.” That's the part of hiring an electrician people worry about most: what happens after the first visit.

Linnebur Electric is family owned and operated, with License #1353 printed on every page of our site. We keep a smaller staff for continuity between projects, and all of our employees routinely attend continuing education classes. Three of them are Master Electricians with at least 25 years of experience, according to our about page.

sections.quote: Rod and his crew are absolutely a pleasure to work with. Open, honest and responsive for all your needs. They’ve went above and beyond for me in every aspect. I HIGHLY recommend them for all your needs. Commercial or residential

sections.quote: I want you to know how appreciative I am that they were able to come and complete my job way before I expected it to happen.  The technician that did the demonstrated great confidence and expertise in what he was doing.  I highly recommend Linnebur Electric.

sections.heading: A Happy Customer Is a Lifetime Customer
body: That line is on Linnebur's own site, next to two more: "We believe in doing the job right the first time," and "We believe you don't have to sacrifice quality for a fair price."
Ken M. wrote that the job was finished "way before I expected it to happen." The reviews are where you can check the slogans.

sections.heading: What Danny D. and Frank B. Wrote
body: Danny D. wrote that "Rod and his crew are absolutely a pleasure to work with," and called them "Open, honest and responsive for all your needs."
Frank B. had "worked with a number of electricians across the state" and wrote that this experience was "by far the best."

sections.heading: From a Kitchen Circuit to a Grain Elevator
body: The services page opens the residential list with "Whether you're starting from the ground up or looking to renovate an existing structure." That list covers new homes, remodels, ceiling fans, LED retro-fits and phone and TV cabling.

On the commercial side we wire offices, restaurants, churches and dental and medical clinics. Industrial runs to "grain elevators and machine shops to truck repair facilities," and the list includes metal building wiring, 3-phase motor control, CNC mill machine wiring and design/build work.

Andale Farmers Coop, Axiom Engineers, Hentzen Contractors, Morton Buildings and Simpson Construction are among the companies we've worked for. Danny D. wrote “Commercial or residential” in his review.

sections.heading: Out of Town for Agricultural Projects
body: We're at 234 S Colorado St in Wichita, and we work across the Wichita area. Linnebur's site says "We've done work in many of the areas around Wichita," and that they enjoy getting out of town for agricultural projects.
If the job is outside the city, call and tell us where it is, and we'll go from there.

sections.quote: Linnebur Electric's quality of work and professionalism are exceptional. Having worked with a number of electricians across the state, this experience has been by far the best. I highly recommend them!

footer.about: Linnebur Electric, Inc. is a family-owned and operated electrical contractor in Wichita. We wire and repair homes, commercial buildings and industrial sites.

why: Your current site is four pages. The homepage headline is just “LINNEBUR ELECTRIC,” with no electrician and no Wichita, and every service sits on one page with the commercial and industrial lists hidden until someone taps. On a phone, the first screen has no phone number, and the Call button is inside the menu.

Your reviews say more than your site does. Dod I.: “These were the only guys how could find the problem and get it fixed.” Danny D.: “Open, honest and responsive for all your needs.” Those words sit on Google, not on your site.

So the demo tells one story: when a problem has been hard to find, you find it. It opens with electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and outdoor lighting a page each. Your site prints License #1353 in the footer, so we kept it.

cards.title: Homepage

fixes: A page for electrical repair in Wichita, KS, built on what customers wrote and what Linnebur's site lists.
Garage and shed outlets, older houses and commercial buildings answered on the page.
cards.alsoAdd: Outlet Installation, Ceiling Fan Installation and LED Lighting Retro-Fits pages, plus commercial and industrial pages, each built for its own search.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your homepage says “over 30 years” while your about page says “Since 1982,” so which one should every listing use?
Your footer reads “LINNEBUR ELETRIC,” your logo reads “LINNEBUR ELECTRIC INC.” and your pages say “Linnebur Electric, Inc.,” so which name should Google and every directory show?
BBB lists Kent Linnebur as president and your site gives his email, while a Google review thanks “Rod and his crew,” so who should the site name as the person customers reach?

lead.heading: Why we led with finding the problem
lead.text: We led with finding the cause because it's built on things Google can't find anywhere else: your real reviews, in your customers' own words. Dod I. said you were the only electricians who could find a problem that several others couldn't, and that story lives nowhere else on the web. The jobs your customers name, like a 44-year-old home or a pool and backyard, are Wichita specifics no generic electrician page can copy.
